correctness.rationale: Condition on the endpoint W_H=y. Brownian bridge reversal in the damped sup norm couples to e^(−u/2)(y+B_u) with error bounded on [0,H] by O((|x_H|+|y|+|B_H|)/H); the tails beyond H vanish because of the exponential damping. Both statistics are Lipschitz in sup norm (constants 1 and 2), and the path includes 0 in its closure, so the endpoint is restricted to |y|≤r on the event. On bounded endpoint sets the scaled Gaussian density tends uniformly to 1/√(2π) for |x_H|=o(√H). Sandwiching in r works at continuity points of the integrated distribution function. For transfer, the critical ERW conditional drift is S_k/(2k); the martingale increment is a_{k+1}(ξ_{k+1}−S_k/(2k)), so Azuma with sum of squared increment bounds O(log ℓ) makes |M_ℓ|>H^(1/4) negligible. The cited conditional clock estimate with ℓ=ceil((log n)^16), r=1 and threshold H^(−4) gives O(H^(−8)) conditional error on the good starts. Independently, the same rate follows from embedding each increment by exit from a Brownian interval with endpoints −a_{k+1}(1+S_k/(2k)) and a_{k+1}(1−S_k/(2k)). Its time has conditional variance O(a_{k+1}^4) and mean a_{k+1}^2(1−(S_k/(2k))^2); Doob bounds the time martingale and the summed conditional mean deficit has expectation O((1+M_ℓ²)/ℓ). Brownian increments after T_ℓ are fresh given the start. The Brownian modulus on an O(H) horizon at mesh H^(−4) is ≤H^(−1) except with probability bounded by a polynomial in H times exp(−cH²); the grid has mesh O(ℓ^(−1)), and the coefficient error is O(ℓ^(−1/2)+L^(−2)) times a Brownian maximum bounded by H² outside a negligible event. The omitted early walk is bounded by ℓ/L and the damped extension is negligible. Thus these errors are genuinely o(H^(−1/2)) in probability of exceptional events, not merely o(1). Nearest-neighbour exit uses absolute maximum threshold 1 after dividing by L; cycle cover uses range threshold 1−1/L. H∼2 log L converts 1/√(2π) to 1/(2√π). Qin's integrable uniform bounds apply to both integer-time tails. Their integral equals the expected time divided by L². Tonelli gives E[J^(−2)] after integrating the profile; the integrals are finite by domination and positive because the limiting Brownian statistics are positive and finite almost surely. The comparison constants follow from M_y≤R_y≤2M_y. No numerical constant or all-time continuity is needed.
